description:
The Amazon Center for Quantum Computing (CQC) in Pasadena, CA, is looking to hire an Applied Scientist in the Quantum Error Correction Theory Team. You will be joining a multi-disciplinary team of scientists working at the forefront of quantum computing. 

The ideal candidate should posses comprehensive knowledge of quantum fault tolerance theory, including: 
- Topological, concatenated and low density parity check codes
- Quantum decoding algorithms
- Fault-tolerant logical protocols
You will contribute to developing hardware-aware fault-tolerant protocols and software tools for performance analysis under realistic noise models, helping guide our organization toward delivering a fault-tolerant quantum computer.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and evaluate novel quantum error correction schemes, including new codes and fault-tolerant protocols
- Research and develop hardware-optimized architectures for fault-tolerant computing
- Drive experimental implementations of quantum fault-tolerance
- Develop simulation and modeling software tools
- Lead high-impact, collaborative research projects aligned with our engineering roadmap
- Apply strong engineering principles while maintaining scientific rigor

A day in the life
Based in Pasadena, CA, you'll work in our purpose-built facility, designed for quantum computing research and development, adjacent to Caltech's campus. As an applied scientist in the quantum error correction team, you will:
- Drive independent research while collaborating on fault tolerance projects within our architecture
- Stay abreadth with current developments in the active field of fault-tolerance through joint Caltech seminars and conference participation
- Partner with experimental scientists to enhance logical performance of quantum processors in a unique opportunity to bridge theory and experiment
- Design error correction schemes optimized for specific quantum algorithms
- Collaborate with control stack engineers to enable increasingly sophisticated fault-tolerance experiments
- Work with systems engineers to identify, understand, and model technical requirements
- Contribute to regular team discussions and joint planning sessions

About the team
